purpose: Close three of the five tenant-bearing tables that had no row policy, and correct a measurement that had gone stale. V8.4.1 asks that a consumer operation NEVER affect a tenant it has no relationship with; the recorded assessment measured the gap as three tables, and measured again on PostgreSQL 16 against the complete forward-only chain it is five of the forty that carry a tenant column. The requirement stays FAIL because two remain.
requiredInvariants: The boundary goes in the forward-only migration chain, not in infra/sql/production-rls-policies.sql. Migration 20260807006000 already states the principle and #4814/#4815 were the same correction: a tenant boundary must not be an accidental property of a later deploy artifact.

deal_events gets a tenancy qualifier only. Copying deal_documents' app_document_deal_authorized would have been a different control: the command path reads the previous event to compute prevHash, and making that read depend on per-deal visibility could break it for a case the migration cannot enumerate. Per-deal visibility on this table is a separate decision with its own evidence.
Append-only on deal_events from 20260712090000 is untouched. The trigger and rules still refuse UPDATE and DELETE; this decides who may read and insert, not whether a row may change.

The two regulatory-integration inbox tables are NOT covered, and the requirement stays FAIL because of them. They are written by the ingest through raw SQL across six repositories and whether that path runs inside the RLS transaction has not been established; enabling row security on an ingest that carries no tenant setting does not protect it, it stops it. Covering three of five and calling the boundary done is the failure this programme keeps finding.
The remaining two are named exclusions in the gate, in source, with the reason. A third uncovered tenant-bearing table fails the gate. There are no silent exclusions.

The two FGIS tables have no runtime caller anywhere in apps/api/src, so their policies are hardening ahead of a first reader rather than a change to live behaviour. Their qualifier is copied from the two siblings in the same migration that did get row security, so all four now agree.
No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. Applying the migration to production is a separate controlled exact-SHA release with its own authority.
acceptance: Measured on PostgreSQL 16 against the complete chain: tenant-bearing tables without a row policy go from 5 to 2, of 40 that carry a tenant column.

The boundary is proven, not asserted: with the context set to tenant A a same-tenant insert succeeds and a cross-tenant insert is refused with 'new row violates row-level security policy'; a read under tenant A returns only tenant A's row, under tenant B only tenant B's, and with no context at all returns nothing.
Dropping the deal_events policies makes the gate raise TENANT_TABLE_WITHOUT_ROW_POLICY:deal_events; re-applying the migration restores PASS, which also shows the migration is idempotent.
The existing inert-policy and blanket-policy checks still pass unchanged.

V8.4.1 stays FAIL and its conditions revoke in both directions: removing the deal_events boundary rejects it, and removing an exclusion from the gate - which is what closing the remaining gap entails - also rejects it.

The revocation condition was rewritten twice. The original asserted the absence of 'row level security' in migration 20260712090000, a file that is applied and must never be edited, so it could never have revoked. Its replacement was an ABSENT_IN_TREE over the migrations directory - and that evaluator reads only .ts/.tsx/.js/.jsx/.mjs/.cjs, never .sql, so it scanned zero files and held unconditionally. Caught by mutation, removed rather than reworded, because the gate condition already carries that revocation and is proven to.
